sets.name: Pinball UI
sets.made: Photographed parts, a live chrome ball, recorded sounds
sets.tagline: Ordinary controls as real pinball parts. A switch whose knob is a chrome ball kicked onto a lamp, a send button you pull back like a shooter rod, delete as the drain with SHOOT AGAIN to undo.

sets.name: Cockpit UI
sets.tagline: Ordinary controls as the cockpit of a 1990s giant-robot anime. A confirm button you hold until the robot launches, a slider that is a dial, an AI agent's status as a turning hologram.

sets.name: Rubber Hose UI
sets.made: Painted bodies, limbs drawn in code
sets.tagline: Ordinary controls as a 1930s rubber-hose cartoon. Every control is a character: the button gets bopped, the slider is a trombone, the toast is a toaster.

sets.name: Sakuga VFX
sets.made: Effects drawn in code on one canvas
sets.tagline: Ordinary controls that react like anime. Plain at rest; use one and it squashes on springs and throws smoke, impact bursts and manga sound-effect lettering.

sets.name: Pixel Worlds
sets.tagline: Ordinary controls with a small living pixel-art scene inside them. The control's value drives the scene: hold delete and a dragon breathes fire across the button.

components.name: toggle
components.title: Toggle
components.description: A switch whose knob is a chrome pinball in a short lane. Flip it and the ball is kicked across, hits the far wall, rocks in its seat and settles, and the lamp under the on end lights.
components.docs: Pinball UI Toggle is a plain script that registers a custom element. Load /pinball-ui/toggle.js with a script tag (not a module), then use <pinball-toggle></pinball-toggle>. Read el.checked and listen for change. Works in forms with a name, like a checkbox. Size it with --pb-size.

components.name: slider
components.title: Slider
components.description: A slider whose thumb is a chrome pinball rolling along a lane of ten lamps. Each lamp lights as the ball reaches it and goes out as the ball rolls back past it, so the lit lamps are the filled part of the track.
components.docs: Pinball UI Slider is a plain script that registers a custom element. Load /pinball-ui/slider.js with a script tag (not a module), then use <pinball-slider value="40" min="0" max="100"></pinball-slider>. Read el.value; it fires input while it moves and change when let go. Works in forms with a name. Size it with --pb-size.

components.name: plunger
components.title: Plunger
components.description: A send button you pull. It is a bare pinball shooter rod: knob, rod, spring and rubber tip. Pull the knob all the way back and a ball drops in front of the tip; let go and the plunger knocks the ball off the edge of the screen and fires send.
components.docs: Pinball UI Plunger is a plain script that registers a custom element. Load /pinball-ui/plunger.js with a script tag (not a module), then use <pinball-plunger label="Send"></pinball-plunger>. Listen for send; el.fire() does a full pull for you. Size it with --pb-size.

components.name: stepper
components.title: Stepper
components.description: A number stepper made of two pinball flippers either side of a two-digit score reel. Press a flipper and it snaps up, the lamp flashes and the drums roll to the new number, carrying into the tens like an old score counter.
components.docs: Pinball UI Stepper is a plain script that registers a custom element. Load /pinball-ui/stepper.js with a script tag (not a module), then use <pinball-stepper value="4" min="0" max="99"></pinball-stepper>. Read el.value; it fires input and change. Works in forms with a name. Size it with --pb-size.

components.name: targets
components.title: Drop targets
components.description: A row of up to four checkboxes as a bank of pinball drop targets with your labels printed on them. Tick one and a ball rolls in, knocks its target down and lights its lamp; untick it and the target springs back up. Knock all four down for a bonus chime.
components.docs: Pinball UI Drop targets is a plain script that registers a custom element. Load /pinball-ui/targets.js with a script tag (not a module), then use <pinball-targets items="EMAIL,PUSH,TEXT,CALLS" checked="0,2"></pinball-targets>. Read el.selected (the ticked items) or el.checked (an array of booleans); it fires change and, when all are ticked, bonus. Works in forms with a name. Size it with --pb-size.

components.name: drain
components.title: Drain
components.description: A delete button with an undo window, built from a pinball outhole and a SHOOT AGAIN lamp. Press or drag the ball into the drain to delete; SHOOT AGAIN blinks while you can still undo, and pressing it kicks the ball back out.
components.docs: Pinball UI Drain is a plain script that registers a custom element. Load /pinball-ui/drain.js with a script tag (not a module), then use <pinball-drain window="6000" label="Delete draft"></pinball-drain>. Listen for delete, undo and commit (the delete is final); el.reset() serves a new ball. Size it with --pb-size.

components.name: bumper
components.title: Pop bumpers
components.description: Pinball pop bumpers as buttons.
components.docs: Pinball UI Pop bumpers is a plain script that registers a custom element. Load /pinball-ui/bumper.js with a script tag (not a module), then use <pinball-bumper cap="+1"></pinball-bumper> for one button, or <pinball-bumpers caps="100,500,100"></pinball-bumpers> for the cluster. Both fire hit with { points, score, combo }. Size it with --pb-size.

components.name: launch
components.title: Launch
components.description: A red button under an orange guard. Lift the guard, then hold the button: lamps count up, the screen counts down, speed lines close in. Hold to the end and the robot launches across the whole control.
components.docs: Cockpit UI Launch is a plain script that registers a custom element. Load /cockpit-ui/launch.js with a script tag (not a module), then use <cockpit-launch></cockpit-launch>. Listen for cockpit:launch; read el.state (safe, armed, launched); el.reset() puts the guard back. Put it on a dark background.

components.name: dial
components.title: Output gain
components.description: A slider that is a dial beside a screen. Turn it and eleven lamps light round it, the number and the trace on the screen climb, and the copy changes at each level. At 100 the pilot cuts in.
components.docs: Cockpit UI Output gain is a plain script that registers a custom element. Load /cockpit-ui/dial.js with a script tag (not a module), then use <cockpit-dial value="20"></cockpit-dial>. Read el.value (0 to 100); it fires input while it turns and change when let go. Works in forms with a name. Put it on a dark background.

components.name: checklist
components.title: Pre-launch check
components.description: Four latching buttons with lit labels and a screen that keeps the tally. Tick all four and the deck crew wave you off.
components.docs: Cockpit UI Pre-launch check is a plain script that registers a custom element. Load /cockpit-ui/checklist.js with a script tag (not a module), then use <cockpit-checklist></cockpit-checklist>. Read el.value (four digits such as "1010") and el.complete; it fires input and change. Works in forms with a name. Put it on a dark background.

components.name: lock
components.title: Safety lock
components.description: A heavy toggle between LOCK and RELEASE beside a screen listing four clamps. Throw it and the clamps let go one after another; when the last one goes, the restraints blow off.
components.docs: Cockpit UI Safety lock is a plain script that registers a custom element. Load /cockpit-ui/lock.js with a script tag (not a module), then use <cockpit-lock></cockpit-lock>. Read el.checked and listen for change. Works in forms with a name. Put it on a dark background.

components.name: mode
components.title: Drive mode
components.description: Four key caps: cruise, combat, snipe, stealth. The chosen one lights in its own colour and the screen redraws for it. Choosing combat brings the robot's fist.
components.docs: Cockpit UI Drive mode is a plain script that registers a custom element. Load /cockpit-ui/mode.js with a script tag (not a module), then use <cockpit-mode></cockpit-mode>. Read el.value (cruise, combat, snipe or stealth); it fires input and change. Works in forms with a name. Put it on a dark background.

components.name: alert
components.title: Alert
components.description: A warning panel: three level lamps, a hazard-striped window and an ACKNOWLEDGE bar. It shows a notice, a caution or a warning; a warning flashes red and brings the missiles.
components.docs: Cockpit UI Alert is a plain script that registers a custom element. Load /cockpit-ui/alert.js with a script tag (not a module), then use <cockpit-alert></cockpit-alert> and call el.show("warning", "Disk almost full"). Listen for cockpit:ack; read el.level. Put it on a dark background.

components.name: tabs
components.title: Monitor select
components.description: Three key caps over a monitor: main, sub and rear. Changing tab cuts through static. Stay on the rear camera for a moment and a contact turns up.
components.docs: Cockpit UI Monitor select is a plain script that registers a custom element. Load /cockpit-ui/tabs.js with a script tag (not a module), then use <cockpit-tabs></cockpit-tabs>. Read el.value (main, sub or rear); it fires input and change. Put it on a dark background.

components.name: agent
components.title: Agent state
components.description: A status display for an AI agent. The robot stands as a hologram on a projector base and turns; its pose and colour follow the state (standby, thinking, working, waiting, done, error) and a window names the task.
components.docs: Cockpit UI Agent state is a plain script that registers a custom element. Load /cockpit-ui/agent.js with a script tag (not a module), then use <cockpit-agent></cockpit-agent> and call el.set("working", "reading 12 files"). States: standby, thinking, working, waiting, done, error. It fires cockpit:state. Put it on a dark background.

components.name: loading
components.title: System load
components.description: A long gauge with a segmented bar and a number window. Feed it progress and the line under it reports what is starting up; at 100 the robot's visor lights.
components.docs: Cockpit UI System load is a plain script that registers a custom element. Load /cockpit-ui/loading.js with a script tag (not a module), then use <cockpit-loading></cockpit-loading> and call el.set(0.4) with progress from 0 to 1. Add the demo attribute to make it run by itself. It fires cockpit:done at 100. Put it on a dark background.

components.name: stepper
components.title: Active time
components.description: Minus and plus keys round an amber window, with a strip of ten lamps. Each press is thirty seconds; hold to repeat. At five minutes the power cable comes out.
components.docs: Cockpit UI Active time is a plain script that registers a custom element. Load /cockpit-ui/stepper.js with a script tag (not a module), then use <cockpit-stepper value="120"></cockpit-stepper>. Read el.value in seconds (30 to 300); it fires input and change. Works in forms with a name. Put it on a dark background.

components.name: input
components.title: Callsign
components.description: A real text field in a long green window, with a character count and a small speaker screen. Typing rattles the keys; Enter registers the name and the bridge answers.
components.docs: Cockpit UI Callsign is a plain script that registers a custom element. Load /cockpit-ui/input.js with a script tag (not a module), then use <cockpit-input></cockpit-input>. Read el.value; it fires input, change, and cockpit:enter with { value } when Enter is pressed. Works in forms with a name. Put it on a dark background.

components.name: button
components.title: Button
components.description: A button who is a red dome with a grin. Press him and a gloved fist comes down and flattens him, with stars and BOP!; let go and he springs back black-eyed and bandaged, with birds going round his head.
components.docs: Rubber Hose Button is a plain script that registers a custom element. Load /rubber-hose-ui/button.js with a script tag (not a module), then use <hose-button>Confirm</hose-button>. Listen for click; type="submit" submits its form. The text inside is its accessible name and is not shown.

components.name: toggle
components.title: Toggle
components.description: A switch whose knob is a lightbulb. Off, he is grey and half asleep. Switch it on and he stretches across like taffy, lights up, and throws his fists in the air under a ring of rays, with CLICK!.
components.docs: Rubber Hose Toggle is a plain script that registers a custom element. Load /rubber-hose-ui/toggle.js with a script tag (not a module), then use <hose-toggle label="Lights"></hose-toggle>. Read el.checked and listen for change. Works in forms with a name.

components.name: slider
components.title: Slider
components.description: A slider who is a trombone. His slide is the track and his own gloved hand on its handle is the thumb. Notes come out of the bell while it moves, and a fast pull gets a TOOT!.
components.docs: Rubber Hose Slider is a plain script that registers a custom element. Load /rubber-hose-ui/slider.js with a script tag (not a module), then use <hose-slider value="35" label="Volume"></hose-slider>, with min, max and step. Read el.value; it fires input and change. Works in forms with a name.

components.name: checkbox
components.title: Checkbox
components.description: A checkbox who is a square fellow with a blank front. Tick him and his own arm swings round and slaps the check mark on, with ink flying and SPLAT!. Untick him and he wipes it off in a puff.
components.docs: Rubber Hose Checkbox is a plain script that registers a custom element. Load /rubber-hose-ui/checkbox.js with a script tag (not a module), then use <hose-checkbox>Remember me</hose-checkbox>. Read el.checked and listen for change. Works in forms with a name. The text inside is its accessible name and is not shown.

components.name: radio
components.title: Radio
components.description: A radio group of round faces, one to a choice. The chosen one is blue, wide awake and bouncing; the others are cream and dozing off. Pick a sleeper and he pops awake with POP! while the last one nods off.
components.docs: Rubber Hose Radio is a plain script that registers a custom element. Load /rubber-hose-ui/radio.js with a script tag (not a module), then use <hose-radio label="Plan"><option value="a" selected>Option A</option><option value="b">Option B</option></hose-radio>. Read el.value and listen for change. Works in forms with a name.

components.name: input
components.title: Text input
components.description: A text field with a fountain pen standing on it. His nib sits on the caret: he goes wherever the caret goes, hops when a letter lands and flicks ink off his nib.
components.docs: Rubber Hose Text input is a plain script that registers a custom element. Load /rubber-hose-ui/input.js with a script tag (not a module), then use <hose-input label="Name" placeholder="Type something…"></hose-input>. Read and set el.value; it fires input and change. Works in forms with a name.

components.name: tabs
components.title: Tabs
components.description: Folder tabs on a rail. The active one is alive: he stands up out of the rail with his fists in the air and his legs kicking underneath. Pick another and the first drops back while the new one pops up.
components.docs: Rubber Hose Tabs is a plain script that registers a custom element. Load /rubber-hose-ui/tabs.js with a script tag (not a module), then use <hose-tabs label="Sections"><option>Home</option><option>Profile</option></hose-tabs>, two to four tabs. Listen for change (e.detail: index, value, label) and show the panel yourself.

components.name: progress
components.title: Progress
components.description: A loading bar who is a thermometer lying on his side, propped up on his hands. The red climbs his tube while he strains and sweats; at a hundred he lets out a PHEW! and throws his fists up.
components.docs: Rubber Hose Progress is a plain script that registers a custom element. Load /rubber-hose-ui/progress.js with a script tag (not a module), then use <hose-progress label="Loading"></hose-progress> and call el.set(n) with progress from 0 to 1. Listen for hose:done (fires once). el.reset() for the next task.

components.name: rating
components.title: Rating
components.description: Five stars in a chorus line. The ones you have given are yellow, laughing and kicking in time; the rest are pale and asleep. They wake one after another when the score goes up, with POP!.
components.docs: Rubber Hose Rating is a plain script that registers a custom element. Load /rubber-hose-ui/rating.js with a script tag (not a module), then use <hose-rating label="Rating"></hose-rating>. Read el.value (0 to 5) and listen for change. Works in forms with a name.

components.name: toast
components.title: Toast
components.description: A notification who is a toaster. Call show() and he hops up, braces, shakes, and a slice of toast with the message written on it jumps out of his slot, with DING!.
components.docs: Rubber Hose Toast is a plain script that registers a custom element. Load /rubber-hose-ui/toast.js with a script tag (not a module), put <hose-toast></hose-toast> where toasts should appear and call el.show("Saved!"). It stays for the duration attribute (3.6 s) or until el.hide().

components.name: tooltip
components.title: Tooltip
components.description: A help button with a bird behind it. Point at the question mark, focus it or tap it, and the bird pops up towing the hint on a balloon, with TWEET!.
components.docs: Rubber Hose Tooltip is a plain script that registers a custom element. Load /rubber-hose-ui/tooltip.js with a script tag (not a module), then use <hose-tooltip text="Helpful hint!"></hose-tooltip>. Opens on hover, focus and tap; Escape closes it.

components.name: button
components.title: Button
components.description: A button that reacts like an anime impact frame: it squashes when pressed, inverts for one frame on release, and a burst goes off behind it with clouds and ドン!. A secondary variant is quieter.
components.docs: Sakuga Button is a plain script that registers a custom element. Load /sakuga-vfx/button.js with a script tag (not a module), then use <sakuga-button>Confirm</sakuga-button> (variant="secondary" for the quiet one). Listen for click; call el.done() when the action worked to land a check on it.

components.name: toggle
components.title: Toggle
components.description: A switch whose flip is 43 painted frames: the knob smears across, slams into the end, throws up a splash, and the track floods and settles. The frames are inside the file (about 500 KB).
components.docs: Sakuga Toggle is a plain script that registers a custom element. Load /sakuga-vfx/toggle.js with a script tag (not a module), then use <sakuga-toggle label="Notifications"></sakuga-toggle>. Read el.checked and listen for change. Works in forms with a name.

components.name: slider
components.title: Slider
components.description: A range slider whose thumb stretches and lags on a spring, with cumulus rolling up behind a fast drag and a crescent thrown ahead on release.
components.docs: Sakuga Slider is a plain script that registers a custom element. Load /sakuga-vfx/slider.js with a script tag (not a module), then use <sakuga-slider value="30" label="Volume"></sakuga-slider>, with min, max, step and unit. Read el.value; it fires input and change. Works in forms with a name.

components.name: checkbox
components.title: Checkbox
components.description: A checkbox that slashes: crescents swing round the box, crystals fly, the tick draws itself, and ズザッ lands in dotted letters.
components.docs: Sakuga Checkbox is a plain script that registers a custom element. Load /sakuga-vfx/checkbox.js with a script tag (not a module), then use <sakuga-checkbox>Remember me</sakuga-checkbox>. Read el.checked and listen for change. Works in forms with a name.

components.name: radio
components.title: Radio
components.description: A radio group whose picked dot springs in with a fan of wedges, two puffs and a hollow ポン.
components.docs: Sakuga Radio is a plain script that registers a custom element. Load /sakuga-vfx/radio.js with a script tag (not a module), then use <sakuga-radio label="Plan"><option value="a" selected>Option A</option><option value="b">Option B</option></sakuga-radio>. Read el.value and listen for change. Works in forms with a name.

components.name: input
components.title: Input
components.description: A text field that kicks up a puff of dust from the caret on every key.
components.docs: Sakuga Input is a plain script that registers a custom element. Load /sakuga-vfx/input.js with a script tag (not a module), then use <sakuga-input label="Name" placeholder="Type something"></sakuga-input>. Read and set el.value; it fires input and change. Works in forms with a name.

components.name: tabs
components.title: Tabs
components.description: Tabs where the raised tab slides to the one you pick, stretching, and lands with wedges and a puff.
components.docs: Sakuga Tabs is a plain script that registers a custom element. Load /sakuga-vfx/tabs.js with a script tag (not a module), then use <sakuga-tabs label="Sections"><option>Home</option><option>Profile</option></sakuga-tabs>. Listen for change (e.detail: index, value, label) and show the panel yourself.

components.name: progress
components.title: Progress
components.description: A loading bar with a storm cloud riding its leading edge, pebbles lifting off the ground and ゴゴゴゴ; at the end a burst, ドン! and a check.
components.docs: Sakuga Progress is a plain script that registers a custom element. Load /sakuga-vfx/progress.js with a script tag (not a module), then use <sakuga-progress label="Loading"></sakuga-progress>, then el.set(n) with progress from 0 to 1. Listen for sakuga:done (fires once). el.reset() for the next task.

components.name: rating
components.title: Rating
components.description: Five stars that pop in one after another, with wedges and a hollow ポン on the last; five gets a burst.
components.docs: Sakuga Rating is a plain script that registers a custom element. Load /sakuga-vfx/rating.js with a script tag (not a module), then use <sakuga-rating label="Rating"></sakuga-rating>. Read el.value (0 to 5) and listen for change. Works in forms with a name.

components.name: toast
components.title: Toast
components.description: A notification that streaks in as a smear, lands in dust with ズザッ, wobbles and leaves by shrinking.
components.docs: Sakuga Toast is a plain script that registers a custom element. Load /sakuga-vfx/toast.js with a script tag (not a module), then use Put <sakuga-toast></sakuga-toast> where toasts should appear and call el.show("Saved"). It stays for the duration attribute (2.6 s) or until el.hide().

components.name: tooltip
components.title: Tooltip
components.description: A help button whose hint springs out like a speech bubble, with puffs and a hollow カチッ.
components.docs: Sakuga Tooltip is a plain script that registers a custom element. Load /sakuga-vfx/tooltip.js with a script tag (not a module), then use <sakuga-tooltip text="Helpful hint!"></sakuga-tooltip>. Opens on hover, focus and tap; Escape closes it.

components.name: sage
components.title: Sage
components.description: Agent thinking states as a status chip: a pixel-art wizard at his desk who does whatever the agent is doing.
components.docs: Sage is a plain script that registers a custom element. Load /pixel-worlds/sage.js with a script tag, then use <sage-status state="thinking"></sage-status> and call el.set(state, label, detail). States: thinking, searching, reading, running, writing, waiting, done, failed.

components.name: hoard
components.title: Hoard
components.description: A hold-to-delete button with a pixel-art dragon in it. Hold and the fire is the fill; hold to the end and it fires hoard:delete.
components.docs: Hoard is a plain script that registers a custom element. Load /pixel-worlds/hoard.js with a script tag, then use <hoard-button heading="Delete this project" warning="This can't be undone."></hoard-button> and listen for the hoard:delete event.

components.name: raven
components.title: Raven
components.description: A send button with a pixel-art raven in it. He carries the message across the button to a tower window, and that flight is the progress.
components.docs: Raven is a plain script that registers a custom element. Load /pixel-worlds/raven.js with a script tag, then use <raven-send></raven-send>. Set the progress attribute (0 to 1) from your own send, or leave it off for a timed flight on click. Listen for the raven:sent event.

components.name: round
components.title: Round
components.description: A loading bar that is the bar of a tavern: seven pixel-art regulars empty their cups in turn as the task loads.
components.docs: Round is a plain script that registers a custom element. Load /pixel-worlds/round.js with a script tag, then use <round-bar value="0" label="Loading"></round-bar> and call el.set(n) with progress from 0 to 1. Listen for the round:done event.

components.name: keep
components.title: Keep
components.description: A password field where strength is a castle: each keystroke builds more of it, and a raccoon tests what you built.
components.docs: Keep is a plain script that registers a custom element. Load /pixel-worlds/keep.js with a script tag, then use <keep-field></keep-field>. Read el.value and el.score (0 to 1), and listen for the keep:change event.

components.name: sigil
components.title: Sigil
components.description: A loading spinner that is a summoning circle cut into slate-blue stone, with a wisp for a light. With no value the wisp circles the ring; give it a value and the runes charge one by one; at 100% something answers.
components.docs: Sigil is a plain script that registers a custom element. Load /pixel-worlds/sigil.js with a script tag, then use <sigil-spinner label="Loading"></sigil-spinner>. With no value it is a plain spinner. Call el.set(n) with progress from 0 to 1 to fill the arc and charge the runes (a value that stands still shows as waiting), el.set(1) to finish, el.fail() if the task fails, and listen for the sigil:done and sigil:fail events.
